3.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
3.text: "Of course. It's easy to dwell in the past, but it's the present that requires our attention."

4.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
4.text: "Ah, the Battle of Holsord. A tragic moment in our history. I wasn't directly involved, but I saw its devastating effects."

5.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
5.text: "I can still recall the sight of the city in ruins, the people despairing. It was a stark reminder of the cost of war."

6.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
6.text: "The Great Betrayal... It was a dark time, and not only for the monarchists. The entire city was gripped by fear and suspicion."

7.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
7.text: "But we pushed through. Despite the upheaval, the work of rebuilding the capital couldn't be put on hold."

8.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
8.text: "That's what they say. But in my opinion, their flaws outweighed their merits."

9.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
9.text: "The Corps, for instance, established a sense of order that helped the populace recover, but its indoctrination methods were questionable."

10.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
10.text: "As for Sollonomics, it did help stabilize the economy, but it also led to a heavy centralization of power."

11.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
11.text: "It wasn't easy. The USP had a certain way of doing things, and quite a few members saw my reforms as a threat."

12.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
12.text: "But I believed in what I was doing, and I was persistent. Eventually, I managed to win over the number of supporters I needed to overhaul the system."

13.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
13.text: "Winning the leadership was a critical step towards implementing the reforms Sordland so desperately needed."

14.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
14.text: "But we must remember the state the country was in when I took over. We were stagnant, and change was necessary."

15.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
15.text: "Unfortunately, economic reforms often have unintended side effects."

16.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
16.text: "Thank you, Mr. President. I tried my best to use my expertise to benefit the party and the country."

18.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
18.text: "The fresh sea breeze, the energy of the city... it's always so invigorating. Makes you forget about the stuffy old bureaucrats trying to get in the way of your policies."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "A little ironic, isn't it? You escaped the bureaucrats, but by increasing Sordland's reliance on global trade and foreign powers, you traded one set of chains for another."

20.speaker: Player
20.text: "I wish I could escape like that. But I never stop thinking about my duties in Holsord. Even now."

21.speaker: Player
21.text: "I couldn't agree with you more. I really should get out of Holsord more often."

22.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
22.text: "I always used to go here to escape the political pressure in Holsord."

24.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
24.text: "I do miss the capital sometimes. I still remember arriving there fresh from Arcasia, brimming with enthusiasm and ideas."

25.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
25.text: "I think it was that feeling that led me to enter the political sphere in the '40s. I could tell the country was stagnating, and I used my knowledge of free-market reforms to garner support within the USP."

26.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
26.text: "As an engineer, my focus was on the energy infrastructure of Holsord. We had many blackouts back then. It was a challenging time -- the aftermath of the Civil War was still evident everywhere."

27.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
27.text: "But even after winning the party leadership against Soll, my time in office was a continuous struggle to dismantle old USP structures and bring about prosperity."

28.speaker: Narrator
28.text: He looked lost in thought for a moment. Then he continued.

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: Alphonso seemed to retreat into his memories for a moment. A gust of wind rattled the helicopter as he continued.

30.speaker: Player
30.text: "Mr. Alphonso, your political career is well-known. Perhaps we should focus on the present?"

31.speaker: Player
31.text: "Free-market reforms were a significant departure. You couldn't expect the traditionalists in the USP to swallow them whole."

32.speaker: Player
32.text: "So your economic expertise was what gave you the edge against Soll. Quite the feat, I must say."

33.speaker: Player
33.text: "You sound quite proud of your achievements. But what about the effects of your reforms on the common people? Didn't the wealth gap widen during your tenure?"

34.speaker: Player
34.text: "You must have arrived shortly after the Battle of Holsord ended."

35.speaker: Player
35.text: "I understand that those were tumultuous times. The Great Betrayal was not so long in the past, was it?"

36.speaker: Player
36.text: "The State Educators Corps and Sollonomics also played significant roles in the rebuilding of Holsord, didn't they?"

37.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
37.text: "A valid concern, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. But in a globalizing world, complete isolation isn't a viable strategy."

38.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
38.text: "That's no good, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. You can't make the right political decisions if you're never exposed to life outside the bubble."

39.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
39.text: "It does you good, being exposed to life outside the political bubble."

40.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
40.text: "You know, looking at the sea reminds me of an incident from my early days at Gasom."

41.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
41.text: "For me, it shaped my political strategies, making them more people-centric and grounded."

42.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
42.text: "It reminded me of the potential of Sordland, of what our nation could be if we embraced change and diversity as Lachaven has."

43.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
43.text: "We had a big deal with a client from Xina, but a gas tanker broke down mid-journey. The delivery was at risk. It was winter, the seas were rough."

44.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
44.text: "We had two days to get the gas to its destination or we'd lose the client. So, I chartered a small cargo ship, braved the stormy seas, and supervised the transfer of the containers myself."

45.speaker: Player
45.text: "Wow. That story speaks volumes about your dedication to Gasom."

46.speaker: Player
46.text: "Your story is impressive, but shouldn't Gasom have had contingency plans for such situations?"

47.speaker: Player
47.text: "Fascinating. But I hope those incidents aren't too frequent at Gasom."

48.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
48.text: "The whole company is like that. We'll do whatever it takes for our clients."

52.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
52.text: "Take a look, Mr. President. That's the world out there in the Lachaven harbor."

53.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
53.text: "No, of course not. We had a good look at our risk management and strategic planning after that debacle."

54.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
54.text: "You're right, and we learned that lesson the hard way. Since then, we've implemented extensive contingency plans."

55.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
55.text: "Don't worry, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. We've come a long way since then."

56.speaker: Player
56.text: "So Gasom's success hinged on your personal heroics? That's not a sustainable strategy for a corporation, is it?"

60.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
60.text: "I remember when we were negotiating our first international contract. We had engineered new excavation methods, but they were untested, unknown. The other side had many alternatives. They could have chosen any established player, but they chose us, a Sordish company."

61.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
61.text: "That deal put Gasom, and in turn Sordland, on the global map. Now, we're a force to be reckoned with in the energy sector."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "It's not about rejecting Gasom, it's about evaluating the best for Sordland. Not all that glitters is gold, Alphonso."

63.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
63.text: "That may be true. But only shooting stars break the mold."

64.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
64.text: "You didn't just reject a business deal back at Gasom. You rejected a chance to further our nation's reach in the global market."

65.speaker: Player
65.text: "They're over-relying on a single sector. It could leave them vulnerable in the long run."

66.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
66.text: "Why, you ask? Because we were willing to take risks for the greater reward."

67.speaker: Player
67.text: "I respect your perspective, Alphonso. But not every risk guarantees a reward."

68.speaker: Player
68.text: "It's obvious by now that our visions for Sordland differ. I believe in a diversified approach, not just relying on one sector or company."

69.speaker: Player
69.text: "You've built a successful business, Alphonso. But the state isn't a business. The risk is carried by our citizens, not shareholders."

70.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
70.text: "I understand that, Mr. President. But without risk, there's no innovation, no progress."

71.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
71.text: "Diversification is wise, but so is recognizing and capitalizing on our strengths, of which energy is certainly one."

72.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
72.text: "Their extensive offshore oil and gas operations and expansive trade relations are proof that their willingness to seize opportunities, even in the face of adversity, has paid off."

73.speaker: Player
73.text: "Are you suggesting we follow Anraka's model despite our vastly different histories and challenges?"

74.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
74.text: "That doesn't mean we can't apply successful business strategies for the benefit of our citizens."

75.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
75.text: "Look at the Federation of Anrakan Isles. They've successfully leveraged their strengths in sea exploration, resource extraction, and naval technology, and turned their geography into an advantage. "

76.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
76.text: "But perhaps, Mr. President, you don't share the same admiration for Anraka's strategy?"

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "Which of their strategies do you suggest we adapt?"

78.speaker: Player
78.text: "Are you willing to consider other sectors for investment, or is your focus solely on energy?"

79.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
79.text: "I'm not suggesting we copy Anraka's model verbatim, Mr. President."

80.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
80.text: "Well, for one, their focus on offshore extraction and naval technology could be beneficial for us, given our lengthy coastline."

81.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
81.text: "While my focus is on energy, I am not blind to the potential of other sectors. But for now, I believe the energy sector holds the most promise for Sordland's economic growth."

82.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
82.text: "Trust is earned, Mr. President. I hope to earn yours by showing you that I'm committed to Sordland's growth. As for my priorities, I believe business can be a force for good."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "My actions are always guided by my commitment to the Sordish people, not personal gain."

84.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
84.text: "I don't think so. Their diversification within the energy sector and strong international trade network will help mitigate that risk."

85.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
85.text: "I'm only saying that we have much to learn from them."

86.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
86.text: "Also, their willingness to foster strong international trade relations is something we could definitely emulate."

87.speaker: Player
87.text: "Do you ever worry that your focus on profit might come at the expense of the Sordish people?"

88.speaker: Player
88.text: "Your dealings have been under scrutiny before, Alphonso. Can you assure me that your interest in the energy sector isn't self-serving?"

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "Why should I trust you, Alphonso, when you've been known to prioritize business over everything else?"

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "Every decision I've made was in the best interest of Sordland and its citizens."

91.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
91.text: "Of course it's self-serving, Mr. President. I'm a businessman, not a saint. But I also firmly believe that what's good for Gasom is good for Sordland."

92.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
92.text: "Mr. President, I understand the implications of my decisions. I won't pretend I'm not interested in profit, but I firmly believe that a prosperous Gasom means a prosperous Sordland."

93.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
93.text: "While we're on the topic of trust, Mr. President, may I remind you that quite a few of your own decisions have been met with controversy. How do you justify your own actions?"

94.speaker: Player
94.text: "I don't need to justify my actions to you, Mr. Alphonso. You are Sordland's past; I am its future."

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: The helicopter tilted to the right and re-adjusted its course. Serge, sensing the escalating tensions in the cabin, reluctantly interjected.

96.speaker: Serge Wolkner
96.text: "Mr. President, Mr. Alphonso, I may only be a driver, but it seems to me that both of you want to steer Sordland towards a better future. You just disagree on the right road to get there."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "Thank you, Serge. It's good to be reminded that we all share a common goal."

98.speaker: Player
98.text: "Serge, do you believe that our duty to the Sordish people should be our guiding principle?"

99.speaker: Player
99.text: "Serge, your perspective is refreshing, but a bit naive. The world of politics and business isn't as straightforward as driving a car."

100.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
100.text: "You know, Serge, if you ever find yourself weary of the political circus, I could always use a reliable man like you at Gasom. Consider it an open offer."

101.speaker: Serge Wolkner
101.text: "I appreciate the offer, Mr. Alphonso, but serving President Rayne and Sordland is my duty and I am proud of it."

102.speaker: Player
102.text: "Serge is loyal to his duty and to Sordland, Alphonso. I suggest you respect that."

103.speaker: Player
103.text: "Serge, you don't need to answer that. This is not the time or place."

104.speaker: Player
104.text: "Alphonso, I hope you're not trying to poach my staff mid-flight!"

105.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
105.text: "Of course, Mr. President. I meant no disrespect."

106.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
106.text: "I understand, Mr. President. It was just an offer."

107.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
107.text: "Apologies, Mr. President. I didn't mean to overstep."

108.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
108.text: "Just a friendly offer, Mr. President, nothing more."

109.speaker: Player
109.text: "I am glad to see you value Serge's skills, Alphonso. But I need him more than you do."

110.speaker: Player
110.text: "Serge, in your view, is it possible to balance business interests with a commitment to public service?"

111.speaker: Serge Wolkner
111.text: "That's very kind of you, Mr. President. I'm here to serve."

112.speaker: Serge Wolkner
112.text: "I believe so, Mr. President. That's what service means to me."

113.speaker: Serge Wolkner
113.text: "Mr. President, I don't know much about business, but I think it's possible if one's heart is in the right place."

114.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
114.text: "Well said, Serge. I strive to balance my business interests with my commitment to Sordland every day."

115.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
115.text: "And serve you do, Mr. Wolkner. You're as astute as you are competent."

116.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
116.text: "A fine sentiment, Serge. I agree that the Sordish people should always come first."

118.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
118.text: "I appreciate your support, Mr. President. It's reassuring to know that there are others who share my dream of a prosperous Sordland."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "Your reforms had quite a few critics, actually. Some said they directly caused the 1951 recession."

120.speaker: Player
120.text: "I'm not sure any amount of reform could have prevented the recession of '51. Do you think there's a surefire way to stop these crises?"

121.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
121.text: "It's easy to pass judgement in retrospect, Mr. President. At the time, I believed those reforms were necessary for Sordland's economic progress."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "Your rapid privatization plan destabilized key sectors of our economy, leading to the worst recession in our modern history."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "Do you think the economic downturn could have been avoided if the Old Guard hadn't obstructed your reforms?"

127.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
127.text: "You made your dislike of my policies loud and clear when you stole the party leadership out from under me."

128.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
128.text: "Flipping my supporters, snaking your way into my inner circle... I won't lie, it was a hard blow."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: "We did what we had to do to save the party and the country. I hope you can understand that."

130.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
130.text: "I understand why you intervened. I was struggling to maintain control."

131.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
131.text: "Resentment doesn't do anyone any good, Mr. President. What happened, happened."

132.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
132.text: "In the world of politics, we often find ourselves making tough choices for the greater good."

133.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
133.text: "But I do admit they could have been implemented at a more moderate pace."

136.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
136.text: "That's a fair critique, Mr. President. Change can be unsettling, especially when it challenges long-held beliefs."

137.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
137.text: "A valid perspective. Balancing economic growth with social safety is indeed a complex challenge."

138.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
138.text: "Regardless of your motivations, your support during those times was crucial, Mr. President."

139.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
139.text: "I understand your viewpoint, Mr. President. I still believe my reforms were necessary, but I'll be the first to admit they weren't perfect."

140.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
140.text: "I still see myself as a facilitator for change. Someone who can help Sordland navigate the complexities of the global economy."

141.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
141.text: "The resistance from the Old Guard certainly worsened the situation, Mr. President."

142.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
142.text: "Destabilization wasn't my goal. I was trying to attract foreign investment and stimulate competition."

143.speaker: Player
143.text: "Do you still resent me for the way things turned out?"

144.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
144.text: "I still believe I brought Sordland the change it needed. But I acknowledge that not everyone may share this view."

145.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
145.text: "You're correct, Mr. President. The recession was a complex event."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: "You were losing control, Alphonso. My intervention was necessary to steer the party in the right direction."

147.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
147.text: "But addressing systemic corruption, improving bureaucratic efficiency and ensuring transparent governance could be key to preventing further downturns."

148.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
148.text: "If the necessary reforms had been implemented in a timely manner, we might have been able to avert the severity of the recession."

149.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
149.text: "However, I admit that the transition could have been better managed."

150.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
150.text: "But I can't help but wonder if you could have achieved your goals in a less aggressive manner."

151.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
151.text: "It's the future of the country that we need to focus on now."

152.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
152.text: "Was that your motivation? I'm not sure."

153.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
153.text: "Their commitment to natural resource extraction and emphasis on naval engineering are commendable. And as a neutral power, the country offers a counterweight to the battle between United Contana and Arcasia."

154.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
154.text: "Gasom has multiple engineers hired from Anraka too. I believe Sordland could find a valuable partner in Anraka in the coming decade."

155.speaker: Player
155.text: "I see potential for collaboration, particularly in offshore resource extraction and marine conservation. We've got much to learn from them."

156.speaker: Player
156.text: "I'm impressed as well, but it's crucial we remain cautious. Anraka's history of piracy and stringent laws could pose challenges in a potential partnership."

157.speaker: Player
157.text: "We should rather focus on Sordland's own strengths. Our future lies in building a self-reliant economy and bolstering our own industries."

158.speaker: Player
158.text: "Anraka has potential. But isn't Rumburg already a counterbalance to the United Contana-Arcasia power struggle?"

159.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
159.text: "Precisely, Mr. President. It's not just about the economic benefits."

161.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
161.text: "Absolutely, Mr. President. Strengthening our domestic economy is paramount."

162.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
162.text: "Rumburg does indeed possess significant power, Mr. President. But the Queen is far more opposed to United Contana and the CSP than Arcasia and the ATO."

163.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
163.text: "Working together can drive innovation and sustainability for both nations."

164.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
164.text: "While Anraka has its unique complexities, I believe these challenges can be managed with careful diplomacy and mutual respect."

165.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
165.text: "But partnerships with countries like Anraka -- or Rizia, for that matter -- could also serve to enhance our own capabilities."

166.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
166.text: "The dynamics would need to shift significantly before they could serve the same function as Anraka."

167.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
167.text: "These are the kind of factors you need to take into account if you're going to reform the Energy Protection Act, by the way. It might seem minor, but any alteration could shape Sordland's future."

168.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
168.text: "But over time, I realized that his approach wasn't working, and that a new direction was needed."

169.speaker: Player
169.text: "You were part of the USP during Soll's rule. You supported his policies then. What changed?"

170.speaker: Player
170.text: "Do you think the growth and prosperity of Lachaven can be replicated in other parts of Sordland?"

171.speaker: Player
171.text: "It took time for their vision to be realized. They didn't even see it come to full fruition during their lifetimes."

172.speaker: Player
172.text: "The Kingdom was a different era. Do you think its strategies can be applied in our modern-day context?"

173.speaker: Player
173.text: "You may be right. But not all cities have Lachaven's potential or resources."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "It must have been interesting, navigating all the changing political dynamics as an outsider."

175.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
175.text: "You're correct, Mr. President. Yes, I supported Soll's policies early on."

176.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
176.text: "Honestly, the key lies in strategic planning and targeted investments. We need to identify sectors with high growth potential and channel our resources there."

177.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
177.text: "Indeed, Mr. President. While the context has changed, the principles of visionary leadership remain the same."

178.speaker: Player
178.text: "I believe that Lachaven's success today is due to the collective effort of its people, not a deceased monarch."

179.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
179.text: "You're absolutely right, Mr. President. Each city in Sordland has its own unique strengths and challenges. Our strategies must be tailored to leverage these unique attributes."

180.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
180.text: "That's a great point, Mr. President. The key lies in persistence and long-term planning."

181.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
181.text: "But would their efforts have been as strong without those leaders setting the direction?"

182.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
182.text: "It was a truly incredible experience, Mr. President."

183.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
183.text: "Despite the challenges and hardships, there was a sense of purpose, a collective will to rebuild and forge ahead."

184.speaker: Player
184.text: "Sounds like a momentous time to be in Holsord. How did it feel to be part of the transformation of the city?"

185.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
185.text: "The dynamics in Holsord were... complicated, to say the least. It was hard not to get caught in the intricate web of political alliances and business rivalries."

186.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
186.text: "It was a steep learning curve, but it was also an invaluable lesson in understanding the complexities of Sordish politics."

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: Alphonso seemed to retreat into his memories for a moment. A gust of wind rattled the helicopter as he continued.

188.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
188.text: "Getting back to Lachaven... I was thinking about how the whole city displays the vision of King Egmund."

189.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
189.text: "Without the investments that he and his chief architect made, Lachaven wouldn't stand shoulder-to-shoulder with Haelm, Porte Drazon, Konstantium and Falenco today."

190.speaker: Player
190.text: "You speak of escaping from old bureaucrats. But isn't the capitalist system you promoted just another form of bureaucracy? Possibly even the worst form of all, for those less fortunate."

191.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
191.text: "An interesting perspective, {BaseGameText.AlphonsoToPlayer}. Of course capitalism creates disparities."

192.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
192.text: "But it's also an engine for growth and innovation. The challenge, as I see it, is to create a more inclusive capitalism that serves the needs of all Sords."

193.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
193.text: "We need to carve out a path that allows Sordland to benefit from our foreign relations while also maintaining our sovereignty."

200.speaker: Player
200.text: "I didn't campaign for you because of your economic reforms, but because I wanted change by any means necessary."

201.speaker: Player
201.text: "To be honest, I never agreed with your economic reforms. I felt they disproportionately favored the wealthy and neglected the needs of the common people."

202.speaker: Player
202.text: "To be frank, Mr. Alphonso, I didn't campaign for you because I didn't like the direction you were taking the party in. I too wanted change, but not your way."

203.speaker: Player
203.text: "I can tell you now that I didn't support your campaign. I felt that the USP was moving away from its roots and that your free-market reforms were a departure from our values."

204.speaker: Player
204.text: "I'm sure you remember that I campaigned for you. I believed in your economic vision then, just as I do now."

205.speaker: Player
205.text: "Even when I was campaigning for you, I had reservations about your economic platform. I thought there could have been a better balance between free-market principles and social safety nets."

206.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
206.text: "Just as Lachaven's success is tied to its global connectivity, Sordland's wealth is tied to its connection to the world and its skilled, educated workforce."

207.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
207.text: "It's akin to what we're trying to achieve with Gasom. Success isn't built overnight. It's the cumulative result of years of planning, investments, and execution."

211.speaker: Narrator
211.text: From here, it was even more evident what a pivotal role the city of Lachaven played in our international trade. Here, at the so-called "Gateway", was where Sordland opened itself to the global market.

212.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
212.text: "We need to identify our strengths, understand our challenges, and formulate a strategy that leverages our unique advantages. It's about adapting and innovating, not merely replicating."

213.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
213.text: "It's not about a one-size-fits-all approach, but a nuanced strategy that considers the local context."

214.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
214.text: "And of course, we need to create a business environment that encourages innovation and entrepreneurship."

215.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
215.text: "The past may have laid the foundation, but it's the present that builds upon it."

216.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
216.text: "Looking at the global landscape, I see great potential in Anraka. Despite their turbulent history, they've emerged as a beacon of resilience and innovation."

217.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
217.text: "It was disheartening, but there was still a sense in those times that anything was possible."

218.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
218.text: "Still, what I remember most about those times was the sense that truly anything was possible."

219.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
219.text: "Back in those days, there was the sense that truly anything was possible."

220.speaker: Ewald Alphonso
220.text: "Before that, I had the sense that truly anything was possible."

221.speaker: Serge Wolkner
221.text: "You're right, Mr. President. Please excuse my interruption."
